strings.name: Eugene Fama
strings.role: Financial economist · Market efficiency and asset pricing
strings.summary: Starting with statistical studies of stock prices, Fama developed efficient-market research during a long Chicago career. His multifactor models with Kenneth French explain differences in stock returns and have influenced asset pricing, index investing and finance education. He shared the 2013 economics Nobel with Hansen and Shiller. His theories and findings continue to inform debates about information, risk and price predictability.

strings.highlights.h1.title: Efficient-market research
strings.highlights.h1.text: Studied how prices reflect information, influencing index investing and debates on market efficiency.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Fama–French factor models
strings.highlights.h2.text: With French, studied how size, value, profitability and investment relate to returns.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Reflects on finance research
strings.timeline.t1.text: Discussed market efficiency, index funds and his long research career in a Chicago interview.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Co-publishes five-factor model
strings.timeline.t2.text: With French, added profitability and investment factors to extend tests of asset returns.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Shares economics Nobel
strings.timeline.t3.text: Honored with Lars Peter Hansen and Robert Shiller for empirical analysis of asset prices.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Co-publishes factor research
strings.timeline.t4.text: With French, identified market, size and value factors in stock returns.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Reviews efficient-market theory
strings.timeline.t5.text: Published a theory-and-evidence review distinguishing efficiency under different information sets.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Publishes stock-price research
strings.timeline.t6.text: Published studies of stock-price behavior and random walks, advancing an empirical framework for market efficiency.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Earns Chicago doctorate
strings.timeline.t7.text: Completed a PhD on stock-return distributions and time-series properties.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joins Chicago faculty
strings.timeline.t8.text: Began teaching before completing his doctorate, starting a long finance-research career.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Graduates from Tufts
strings.timeline.t9.text: Completed undergraduate studies and entered graduate school at Chicago.
